data.title: How To Spot Bank Impersonation Scams Targeting Texas Gulf Bank Customers
data.excerpt: You're in the middle of your day when a text pops up: "Texas Gulf Bank fraud alert — did you authorize a $2,400 transfer?" It isn't us. Here's how to stay safe.
data.body:
You're in the middle of your day when a text pops up:

*"Texas Gulf Bank fraud alert — did you authorize a $2,400 transfer? Reply or call now to stop it."*

The number shows our name. The link looks close. The message feels urgent.

**It isn't us.**

This kind of message is part of a growing trend of bank impersonation scams, which are becoming more frequent across the Southeast Texas Gulf Coast region.

What happens is that fraudsters pose as bank employees through calls, texts, emails, and fake websites to steal your personal information, access your accounts, or get you to send money to a third party.

The good news: a few simple habits can help protect you from almost all of these scams.

### How Texas Gulf Bank Will Contact You

**We will never:**
- Send a link asking you to log in to online or mobile banking
- Ask for your username, password, token code, wire PIN, or one-time passcode in an unsolicited call, text, or email

If a call, text, or email asks you to click a link or hand over login details "to verify activity," treat it as a scam — even if it uses our name or looks similar to our website.

**To sign in safely, always:**
- Type texasgulfbank.com directly into your browser
- Use our official mobile banking app

### How To Stay Ahead of Bank Impersonation Scams

#### 1. Don't Trust Caller ID
A name or number on your screen is not proof of who is calling. If someone calls claiming to be from Texas Gulf Bank and something doesn't feel right, hang up and call us back using the number on the back of your card or from our official website.

#### 2. Go Directly to Our Website or App
To access online banking, always type our URL directly into your web browser or use our mobile app. Avoid logging in through links in texts or emails.

#### 3. Never Share Login Details or Security Codes
Keep usernames, passwords, token codes, wire PINs, and one-time passcodes to yourself. Texas Gulf Bank will never ask for this information in an unsolicited call, text, or email.

#### 4. Take a Moment Before Acting
If a message makes you feel rushed, pause. Read it carefully. Then contact us through a trusted number if you're unsure.

#### 5. Turn On Two-Factor Authentication
Where available, enable two-factor authentication for an extra layer of protection.

### How To Report Suspicious Messages

If you receive a call, text, or email that claims to be from Texas Gulf Bank and you're not sure it's real, call us at **1-800-467-7216** or stop by any Texas Gulf Bank banking center.

{{cta title="Think something looks suspicious?" body="Call us right away or stop by a branch. Our team can help you confirm whether a message is legitimate." primaryLabel="Call 800.467.7216" primaryHref="tel:8004677216" secondaryLabel="Find a Branch" secondaryHref="/locations/"}}

data.title: Commercial Lending for Real Estate Projects: What to Expect When Applying
data.excerpt: Deciding to purchase, expand, or build a commercial property is a significant step. Here's what to expect from the commercial lending process.
data.body:
Deciding to purchase, expand, or build a commercial property for your business is a significant step. It often comes at a point where your current space no longer supports your operations — or where you see a clear opportunity to grow.

Your company may be asking: _Are we choosing the right location? Can our business support this investment? What should we expect from a lender?_

These are important questions, and having clear answers about commercial lending for real estate can make the process of applying for financing more manageable.

### 5 Factors That Shape the Commercial Lending Experience

#### 1. How Owner-Occupied Real Estate Supports Long-Term Business Growth

Owner-occupied commercial real estate can support your business by aligning your facility with operational needs, positioning your business closer to customers, providing stability compared to rising lease costs, and allowing you to build equity.

#### 2. What Lenders Evaluate When You Apply

Key considerations include cash flow, financial performance, business stability, ownership and leadership experience, and market conditions.

#### 3. How Local Market Knowledge Shapes Your Financing Experience

A lender with local market knowledge can help navigate economic conditions, property considerations, and practical timelines influenced by local development conditions.

#### 4. How Loan Structure Aligns With Your Business Operations

Financing is typically structured to reflect how your business operates today while allowing for future growth. An experienced lender can help structure financing that supports specific business needs.

#### 5. What to Expect During the Application Process

The process generally includes an initial discussion, documentation review, evaluation by the in-house team, and a decision. With a clear understanding of each stage, you can approach the application process with greater confidence.

{{cta}}

### Build Your Company's Future With the Right Financing Approach

At Texas Gulf Bank, our team works with businesses to provide guidance, insights, and financing solutions designed to support growth. [Contact us today](https://www.texasgulfbank.com/contact-texas-gulf-bank/) to have a conversation about commercial lending options for your business.

data.title: Our Financing for Construction Equipment Makes Upgrades More Manageable
data.excerpt: When your construction equipment starts slowing down the job, you feel it immediately. Financing for construction equipment may help you upgrade without straining cash flow.
data.body:
When your construction equipment starts slowing down the job, you feel it immediately. Projects take longer, crews get frustrated, and maintenance costs creep up.

In construction, your equipment is a core part of how your business performs. If it is no longer keeping up, continuing to push through another project with outdated machinery may be costing you more than you realize.

Using outdated equipment, you may be experiencing slower job completion times, frequent repairs, increased strain on crews, difficulty meeting timelines, or inability to meet current safety expectations.

### Why Upgrading Equipment Can Strengthen Your Business

With updated equipment, your company may benefit from more efficient project execution, reduced downtime, improved job site safety, greater confidence when bidding on larger projects, and better long-term cost control.

### Benefits of Pursuing Equipment Financing

- **Preserve Cash:** Spread the cost over time and retain working capital for payroll, materials, and day-to-day expenses.
- **Match Payments to Project Revenue:** Structure financing to align with project timelines and revenue cycles.
- **Access Newer Equipment:** Finance newer machinery with advanced technology and safety features.
- **Support Long-Term Growth:** Bid on larger projects and respond to new opportunities with the right equipment in place.

### What the Process Looks Like at Texas Gulf Bank

Our local lending team will be with you every step of the way: discuss your equipment needs, review financing options, submit documentation, receive a lending decision through our in-house team, and move forward with acquisition.

[Contact our local lenders today](https://www.texasgulfbank.com/contact-texas-gulf-bank/) to get started on the lending process.

data.title: Commercial Real Estate Construction Loans Explained for Texas Companies
data.excerpt: Growing companies often need more space. Commercial real estate construction loans are designed to support businesses during critical growth stages.
data.body:
Across the Southeast Texas Gulf Coast region, growing companies often need more space to support day-to-day activity. Whether expanding operations, building a new facility, or moving from a leased building into an owner-occupied property, you may need financial solutions to support construction.

### What Are Commercial Real Estate Construction Loans?

Commercial real estate construction loans are a type of short-term financing used to fund the development, renovation, or expansion of commercial properties. These loans are specifically structured to support the unique phases of construction.

Instead of receiving the full loan amount upfront, funds are distributed over time as your project progresses through a draw schedule.

### How Commercial Construction Loans Work

- **Planning and Approval:** A lender evaluates the full scope of the project, including costs, timelines, and feasibility.
- **Funding Through a Draw Schedule:** As construction milestones are completed, portions of the loan are released to cover labor, materials, and other expenses.
- **Interest-Only Payments During Construction:** During the build phase, you make interest-only payments to help manage cash flow.
- **Transition to Long-Term Financing:** Once construction is complete, the loan may convert into a term loan or permanent financing.

### What Lenders Look For

Lenders consider your business's financial strength and cash flow, the overall feasibility and timeline of your construction projects, the experience of your builders and contractors, and the long-term value of the completed property.

### Planning for Construction in Texas

Building along the Southeast Texas Gulf Coast comes with its own considerations. When preparing, build flexibility into your timeline and budget, account for potential delays in materials or permitting, and work with lenders who understand regional conditions.

### Find a Local Partner

At Texas Gulf Bank, we take a relationship-based approach. Whether you are building a new property, expanding an existing property, or planning renovation projects, [start a conversation with one of our local lenders](https://www.texasgulfbank.com/contact-texas-gulf-bank/) to discuss financing options.

data.title: Texas Gulf Bank Promotes Jessica Cash to Chief Credit Officer
data.excerpt: When Texas Gulf Bank set out to fill its Chief Credit Officer role, the search reached banks across the country. After a thorough process, the answer turned out to be just down the hall.
data.body:
## Jessica Cash Named Chief Credit Officer of Texas Gulf Bank.

When Texas Gulf Bank set out to fill its Chief Credit Officer role, the search reached banks across the country and drew strong interest from highly qualified candidates. After a thorough and comprehensive process, the answer turned out to be just down the hall.

Texas Gulf Bank (the "Bank") today announced that its Board of Directors has unanimously promoted **Jessica Cash** to Chief Credit Officer, effective immediately. Cash steps into the role after most recently serving as Senior Vice President, Credit Manager, capping a decade-long rise through the Bank's credit function.

Steve Thompson, Chief Executive Officer of Texas Gulf Bank said, "We could have saved ourselves some time by just walking down the hall. The process only confirmed what we already knew. Jessica is an outstanding leader and a steward of our credit culture, and this promotion is well deserved."

Since joining Texas Gulf Bank in 2022, Cash has overseen credit department operations, exercised delegated approval authority on complex and policy-exception credits, and led the design and implementation of the Bank's loan origination system to strengthen underwriting consistency and operational scale. She has also supported the Bank's CECL framework and Board-level reporting, and built a credit analyst training program that has helped develop a consistent, scalable talent pipeline.

Her path to the role spans more than a decade in community banking. Before Texas Gulf Bank, Cash held credit leadership and training roles at Allegiance Bank and served as an Associate National Bank Examiner with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, where she assessed asset quality, financial performance, and regulatory compliance. She holds a B.B.A. in Banking and Financial Institutions from Sam Houston State University, where she graduated Magna Cum Laude, and is currently completing her studies at the Southwest Graduate School of Banking at SMU, where she serves as Vice President of Education for her class with the Bank's sponsorship and support.

In her new role, Cash will lead the Bank's credit strategy and risk governance as the organization continues to grow, aligning credit standards and risk appetite with its long-term objectives and expansion across the greater Houston region.

"I'm honored to step into this role and grateful for the trust the Board and leadership team have placed in me," Cash said. "Texas Gulf Bank has invested in my growth from the beginning, and I look forward to continuing to build a strong credit culture that supports our clients, our team, and the communities we serve."

### About Texas Gulf Bank

Founded in 1913 as Freeport National Bank, Texas Gulf Bank adopted its current name following the introduction of branch banking in Texas. Today, the Bank operates 10 banking centers across Harris, Galveston, Brazoria, and Montgomery Counties. As of December 31, 2025, the Bank reported approximately $695 million in total assets, $488 million in loans, and $612 million in deposits. The Bank's Wealth Management and Trust Group reported approximately $1.4 billion in assets under administration.

data.title: Business Working Capital Loans to Help You Navigate Seasonal Revenue Cycles
data.excerpt: Seasonal revenue cycles are a reality for many businesses. Working capital loans help bridge the gap so you can operate consistently year-round.

cta.title: Ready to talk working capital?
cta.body: Meet with a local loan officer who understands Gulf Coast business cycles and can help structure financing around your cash flow.

data.body:
Seasonal revenue cycles are a reality for many businesses in the Southeast Texas Gulf Coast region. You may experience strong periods of demand followed by slower months, or your revenue may depend on project timelines and client payment schedules.

At the same time, your core expenses — payroll, vendor payments, insurance, and other operating costs — continue regardless.

Business working capital loans are designed to help bridge that gap, giving your company the flexibility to operate consistently while staying focused on growth.

### How Seasonal Revenue Cycles Impact Cash Flow

During slower periods, your business may still need to maintain payroll, cover rent and utilities, and pay suppliers. During peak periods, you may need to invest ahead of revenue. Working capital loans help manage these timing gaps.

### How Different Industries Benefit

- **Construction:** Support payroll between draws, cover upfront material costs, and manage delays without slowing operations.
- **Manufacturing:** Purchase materials, maintain production schedules, and manage the gap between delivery and customer payment.
- **Professional Services:** Bridge gaps between invoicing and collections while receivables are outstanding.

### Competitive deposit options while you grow

Some owners prefer to keep operating reserves in a high-visibility deposit product while they plan the next financing step. Current featured rates:

{{rates}}

### How to Prepare to Apply

Start by reviewing your current financial position. Define how you plan to use the funds. When applying, have your financial statements, tax returns, accounts receivable reports, and cash flow documentation ready.

### What to Expect at Texas Gulf Bank

The process begins with a conversation with one of our local lenders. We aim to understand your business and cash-flow challenges. Once documentation is submitted, our in-house lending team reviews your application and makes a timely decision.

[Contact us today](https://www.texasgulfbank.com/contact-texas-gulf-bank/) to get started on the loan process.
